The new check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is therefore always False for real processes. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally and ignored `ValueError`. In `_ensure_processes_alive`, a process flagged "hang" is no longer killed. `_create_process_for_shards` then starts a second process for the same shards while the hung one is still alive. The same isinstance check in `join()` (around line 346) skips `process.terminate()`, so processes that outlive the timeout are never terminated.
